chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād and al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon him: A man doubts during the Maghrib prayer and does not know whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or three. He said: He should give salām, then stand and add one rakʿah to it. Then he said: By Allah, this is among that which can never be made up for me.

key_terms.الْمَغْرِبِ: the Maghrib salat (prayer), the sunset prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَةً: one rakʿah, a unit of prayer
key_terms.لَا يُقْضَى: it is not made up or compensated
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: he gives salām to conclude the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he doubts whether he prayed two or three rakʿahs in Maghrib prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about doubt in the Maghrib prayer when one is uncertain whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or three. The Imam عليه السلام instructs that he should conclude the prayer with salām and then stand to add one rakʿah, indicating a specific jurisprudential treatment of uncertainty in salat (prayer).
